tasks.short: Read fridge and freezer temperatures, probe food during preparation, record them and act on bad readings.

steps.what: Prep worker reads refrigerators and freezers thermometers at set times: by eye today; after the change wireless sensors log them and the worker checks once a shift that every unit reports
Prep worker probes the core temperature of food during cooling and holding
Prep worker writes readings on the paper hygiene list
Prep worker reports out-of-range readings to the chef and moves the food
Chef checks and signs the week's hygiene lists and files them

tasks.design: Wireless sensors in fridges and freezers log temperatures around the clock into a hygiene-code app ({OTHER}) and alert the team on a missed or out-of-range reading. A Bluetooth probe writes core temperatures into the same app after the worker picks the product, corrective actions go into a short form, and the chef reviews exceptions weekly instead of paging through lists.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper lists were the default way to show compliance, and sensors used to be costly.
tasks.enabler_now: Hygiene-code apps with 24/7 temperature monitoring and missed-measurement warnings are sold today.
tasks.still_hard: Probing food and acting on a bad reading stay hands-on; sensors need batteries, Wi-Fi and calibration.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing food that looks or smells wrong even when the number is fine, and acting at once.

ambition.what: Fridge temperatures watched every few minutes, day and night, so a failing fridge is caught before stock is lost.

tasks.altitude: The worker probes food and acts on alerts; reading fridges and writing lists drop out. The chef reviews exceptions.

reach.task: Record cooling and reheating temperatures for large batches
reach.learn: Whether probe logging fits batch cooking records.

evidence.claim: A Dutch hygiene-code app registers HACCP checks, warns on missed measurements and offers 24/7 temperature monitoring.
EU hygiene law requires records commensurate with the size of the business, kept current and shown to the authority.
In the Netherlands an approved hygiene code can replace an own HACCP plan, and the food authority checks.
An app that logs who recorded what can observe staff behaviour, which needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from taking readings to records signed; equipment repair is outside.
Input contract: storage readings from sensors installed per unit; product list for probe readings set up by the chef in the app; fallback is the paper list.
Records show units and products, not individual staff performance.
Chef time is outside the prep worker's savings.

s1 keeps 10 for the worker's check once a shift that every sensor reports and the unit list is green. s2 probing keeps its full time. s3 keeps 30 for picking the product and confirming each probe reading. s4 keeps 90 because moving the food and writing the corrective action stay; only walking to tell the chef about a storage alarm drops.
unknowns: How many fridges and freezers the kitchen has.
Whether the kitchen has Wi-Fi coverage for sensors.
research_questions: How often do paper lists show gaps at inspection today?

already_counted.description: Prep worker picks the product and confirms each probe reading in the app.

incremental.description: Prep worker responds to sensor alerts that turn out to be door-open spikes.
Chef keeps the product list, thresholds and sensor batteries in order.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the Bluetooth probe is not taken up, so food readings are still written by hand and s3 keeps 65 (33.4); high: sensors and probe log as designed (41.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Report broken equipment and low supplies to the chef, and order needed items from suppliers.

steps.what: Prep worker notices equipment not working or supplies getting low
Prep worker tells the chef or writes it on the kitchen whiteboard today; after the change the worker writes the fault in the form opened by the machine's QR code, with a photo
Prep worker checks the fault report: machine, what is wrong, photo and urgency
Prep worker submits the checked fault report as a ticket to the facility helpdesk
Prep worker checks key stock and writes the order list
Chef checks the final order list on the tablet: items and quantities against the menu plan and the shelves, and the wholesaler for each line
Chef releases the checked order lines for integrated wholesalers to their webshops
Prep worker checks the lines to phone against the chef's checked order: items, quantities and the supplier
Prep worker orders needed items: from the wholesaler's webshop or by phone today; after the change only lines the webshops do not cover go by phone
Chef or facility contact calls the service engineer for faulty equipment
Prep worker chases late deliveries or repairs

tasks.design: A QR code on each machine opens a fault form; the prep worker writes the fault with a photo, checks it and submits it once as a ticket in the facility {HELPDESK}, which notifies the chef. Stock is counted on a tablet against par levels in the stock module of the recipe system ({OTHER}), which drafts the order; the chef checks the order on the tablet and releases the lines for integrated wholesaler webshops on the {PARTNER_PORTAL}, and the prep worker checks and phones the rest, with ticket and delivery status visible for follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Faults and shortages were passed on by voice and whiteboard, and orders were phoned or typed per supplier.
tasks.enabler_now: Helpdesk forms, par-level stock modules and wholesaler webshops with order interfaces are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Small suppliers take only phone orders; judging what is really needed for the coming days stays with the team.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a machine that sounds wrong before it breaks, and knowing what the kitchen will run out of.

ambition.what: Repairs tracked from report to fix, so recurring faults per machine show up in a month.

tasks.altitude: The prep worker reports and counts on a tablet; the chef approves rather than builds orders.

reach.learn: Whether the QR fault form fits the cooks' line.

evidence.claim: Recipe tools link recipes to supplier prices so costs follow price changes.
Par levels, a count and a suggested order are deterministic; the cook adjusts.
A QR code on equipment can open a pre-filled helpdesk form.

assumptions: Boundary: from noticing a fault or shortage to order placed and follow-up done; repairs and receiving are outside.
Input contract: par levels per item set by the chef in the stock module; machine IDs on QR labels created by the facility contact; fallback is the whiteboard and phone.
Scenario: integrated webshops cover about 70% of order lines.
Chef time is outside the prep worker's savings.

Noticing faults, writing the fault report, the checks and the releases keep their full time. s3 keeps 70 because counting the shelves stays and only working out quantities and writing the list drop; checking the draft takes about 4 of its 20. s5 keeps 35 for phoning the 30% of lines the webshops do not cover and fixing failed orders. s7 keeps 60 because the status view replaces calls asking where an order is.
unknowns: Which suppliers accept webshop or interface orders.
research_questions: How long do equipment faults stay open today?

already_counted.description: Prep worker checks the drafted order against what they see on the shelves.

incremental.description: Prep worker replaces damaged QR labels and fixes failed orders.
Chef keeps par levels current; facility contact keeps machine labels current.

approvals.approved_version: The fault report with machine, fault, photo and urgency exactly as checked by the prep worker in s2b, submitted once as a ticket to the facility helpdesk queue; any change needs a new check.
The order lines for integrated wholesalers with items and quantities exactly as checked by the chef in s4, sent once to each named wholesaler's webshop; any change needs a new check.
The remaining order lines with items and quantities exactly as on the chef's checked order and checked by the prep worker in s5c, phoned once to the named supplier; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the webshops cover only about half of the lines, so s5 keeps 60 (19.7); high: 70% of lines go through integrated webshops as assumed (25.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plate cold dishes and hand food to waiters at the pass for the right table.

steps.what: Prep worker plates or portions cold dishes per order ticket
Prep worker reads the kitchen screen to match dishes to tables and courses
Prep worker checks allergy notes on the ticket and marks the plate
Prep worker sets dishes at the pass in table and course order
Prep worker tells the waiters and waitresses a dish is ready: by calling out or walking to the floor today, by bumping the dish on the kitchen screen after the change
Waiter collects the dishes and checks them against the order

tasks.design: Configure the kitchen screen ({OTHER}) to group tickets by table and course and to highlight allergy modifiers; when the prep worker bumps a dish as ready, the waiter's handheld gets a pickup notice for that table. Plating and the check at the pass stay manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Kitchens without screens shouted orders; with screens, pickup still relied on calling waiters.
tasks.enabler_now: Kitchen screens and waiter handhelds on the same till can pass ready notices as a setting.
tasks.still_hard: Plating and the final look at each plate are physical; a busy pass still needs voice.
tasks.human_edge: Getting each plate right and keeping calm when tickets pile up.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; less shouting and waiting at the pass.

reach.task: Pick up dishes at the pass
reach.learn: Whether pickup notices cut the time dishes wait.

evidence.claim: Kitchen screens can group tickets by table and send ready notices to waiters' handhelds.
Allergen information for non-prepacked food is mandatory and the operator stays responsible for its accuracy.

assumptions: Boundary: from the ticket to the dish handed to the waiter; serving at the table is outside.
Input contract: tickets with table, course and allergy modifiers, entered by waiters as fixed modifiers in the till when ordering; fallback is the printed ticket.
The kitchen already has a screen; where it has only printers, the pickup notice still needs configuring.
Waiter time is outside the prep worker's savings.

Plating, the allergy check and setting dishes at the pass keep their full time. s2 keeps 90 because grouping by table saves some searching on the screen. s4b keeps 30 for the bump itself and calling waiters who miss the notice. The bump is an ordinary mark on the same kitchen screen, so it needs no approval.
unknowns: Whether the till supports ready notices to handhelds.
Whether waiters enter allergies as fixed modifiers.
research_questions: How long do plated dishes wait at the pass today?

incremental.description: Prep worker sorts out missed bumps and dishes a waiter did not pick up after a notice.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: waiters stand at the pass or do not carry handhelds on all shifts, so the worker still calls for many dishes and s4b keeps 65 (5.3); high: waiters act on the pickup notice (9.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Ring up items at the canteen or deli till, take payment, give correct change and count the drawer.

steps.what: Prep worker operates the cash register: scans packaged items, keys fresh items, weighs salads
Customer pays by card, phone, staff badge or cash
Prep worker takes cash, handles money and counts out correct change
Prep worker sorts out declined cards or badges without balance
Prep worker counts the drawer after service and fills the cash sheet
Catering manager checks the cash sheet and banks the takings

tasks.design: Link the salad-bar scale to the {OTHER} point-of-sale till so weighed items price themselves, and, where the client agrees, run the staff restaurant cashless with card, phone and staff-badge payment. A small float stays for visitors during a transition; the till's own closing replaces most of the cash sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Canteens kept cash for visitors and habit, and scales were not linked to tills.
tasks.enabler_now: Most tills support linked scales, and staff badges and contactless cards cover nearly all canteen payments.
tasks.still_hard: Going cashless is a client and policy decision; some visitors still bring cash.
tasks.human_edge: Serving quickly and kindly at peak, and sorting out a payment problem without a queue building.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; less cash handling and counting.

reach.learn: Whether cashless operation works outside a staff restaurant.

evidence.claim: Tills can price weighed items from a linked scale and take staff-badge payments.
Whether a business may refuse cash, and how badge payments are deducted from pay, follow national rules and need prior notice and agreement.
Badge payment logs are personal data of employees under GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from ringing up items to takings handed over; banking is outside.
Input contract: price per kilo per salad type set by the catering manager in the till; staff badges issued by the client's facility team; fallback is manual weighing and cash.
Scenario: the client agrees to a cashless staff restaurant after notice; 20% cash handling remains in the first year.
Customer and manager time is outside the prep worker's savings.
unknowns: Whether the client will allow cashless payment.
research_questions: How fast does cash use fall after a cashless notice in staff restaurants?

incremental.description: Prep worker explains the cashless policy to visitors and handles exceptions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the client keeps cash, so cash handling stays and the till closing only fills the sales totals on the cash sheet (9.8); high: the restaurant goes cashless with 20% cash left in the first year (39.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The prep worker keeps preparing, plating, probing and serving; reading fridges, lists, calls and cash shrink.
skills_to_grow: Acting on sensor and probe alerts
Counting against par levels on a tablet
Reporting faults with a clear photo and note
role.ambitious_version: A prep worker whose temperature, stock and fault records are always complete, so the kitchen passes inspection and rarely runs out.
